content:
{'index': 0, 'translation': 'King Sir\'s last play I mentioned was "Cyrano de Bergerac," which he translated and directed in 1987. The talented and proud swordsman Cyrano, with his big nose, was both timid and insecure when facing his beloved cousin Roxane. In 2015, when I interviewed James Wong (詹瑞文), I asked him:'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': '"Does a person who has talent feel inferior because of a big nose?"'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': '"Only when they fall in love. Normally they don\'t, but once love arrives, they become a fragile little boy. Love is so childish." (recorded)'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': "It is precisely because his nose is different that Cyrano feels inferior. Love sometimes makes people fragile — we only accept others' strengths, never their weaknesses. That is human nature, and it is also drama. Both life and drama need sublimation. James Wong said this is the last romantic drama of France. An ugly man writes love letters on behalf of a handsome man to the woman he adores — like many things in the world, appearance and truth are forever entangled; though clearly false, it is not without sincerity. What the woman loves is the soul poured into the words (to be continued)."}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'James Wong explained the story\'s background: "After Cyrano is ambushed and wounded in the head, he still visits his cousin every week. His cousin does not know he is deeply in love with her. He writes letters to court his cousin on behalf of that handsome man. Just as the handsome man wants to confess that the letters were not written by him — because the woman says she loves his talent — at the moment of confession, Christian is killed in battle. His cousin takes the letter and enters a convent. Cyrano visits every week, telling her the news from outside, chatting about life (to be continued).'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'Are not half of the most beautiful stories in life lies?'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'The handsome Christian tries to pick up his pen on the battlefield to clarify the truth, but is immediately shot dead; blood stains the letter paper; yet the tears on the paper belong to Cyrano. Blood and tears are equally real, and their coexistence does not stem from the same person. The good and bad in life — if you are unwilling to bear them together, you may ultimately lose them all. "Everyone has their own wounds" — when I saw the finale of the original play, Cyrano, seriously wounded in the head after an ambush, comes to the convent to find his cousin Roxane.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'He takes out from his bosom that letter stained with fresh blood and tears — the one Roxane had always believed was written to her by Christian. She agrees to let Cyrano read it aloud. Cyrano takes the letter and begins: "Goodbye, Roxane, I am going to die. The love I never spoke weighs heavy on my heart. My eyes can no longer greedily gaze upon your every move. Every time I think of you speaking, your fingers lightly touching your cheek — that gesture is so familiar to me that it is unbearable. My heart cries out: goodbye!"'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': '"You read that letter so well, as if..." Roxane said.'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': '"My life, my love, my treasure, my dearest — my heart has always been buried between every beat of yours."'}

{'index': 10, 'translation': "The convent is dimly lit, and Cyrano could not possibly see the contents of the letter — this is precisely the play's flaw. Yet his familiar voice reading the love letter allows Roxane to recognize the voice of the soul she has always loved deeply:"}

{'index': 11, 'translation': '"That person was actually you!"'}

{'index': 12, 'translation': '"No, Roxane, no!"'}

{'index': 13, 'translation': '"Every time you called my name, I should have known."'}

{'index': 14, 'translation': '"No, it\'s not me!" "It\'s you!" "I swear!"'}

{'index': 15, 'translation': '"Now I finally see through this generous lie — those love letters were all written by you!"'}

{'index': 16, 'translation': '"No!"'}

{'index': 17, 'translation': '"Those sweet words, that crazy love, it was all you!"'}

{'index': 18, 'translation': '"No!"'}

{'index': 19, 'translation': '"What moved me in the dark was that voice!"'}

{'index': 20, 'translation': '"I swear, you have got the wrong person!"'}

{'index': 21, 'translation': '"That soul — it is yours!"'}

{'index': 22, 'translation': '"I have never loved you!" "You loved me!"'}

{'index': 23, 'translation': '"No, it was him!"'}

{'index': 24, 'translation': '"You loved me!"'}

{'index': 25, 'translation': '"No!" (his voice growing weaker)'}

{'index': 26, 'translation': '"Your voice is trembling, your denials growing weaker!"'}

{'index': 27, 'translation': 'Drama is falling in love with someone, having the words on the tip of your tongue yet unable to speak them, left with nothing but a "no" — the more you deny, the weaker and more flustered your heart becomes. Drama is falling in love with someone, unable to confess, a lifetime\'s fate twisted and rewritten. Drama is falling in love with someone, knowing you cannot hold on, yet finding a road of deep affection through words and soul. Drama is a lifetime wrestling with light and shadow, sorrow and joy, falsehood and truth. When Roxane discovers that the true author of the love letters is the dying Cyrano, she says: "I loved one person, yet lost him twice (to be continued).'}

{'index': 28, 'translation': 'Life slips away quietly, so quietly it cannot be noticed or controlled. Two men who deeply loved her — in the end neither could possess her — that is drama. What she truly loved was a soul, yet she lost him twice: the first time when Christian was killed in battle; the second when, upon discovering Cyrano was the true author of the letters, Cyrano died in her arms. The dialogue is like poetry — that too is drama.'}

{'index': 29, 'translation': '"The last few lines are also wonderful. When I pass the threshold of God, I will sweep away all the stars on the lintel; the only thing flawless is the proud white feather on my head. So majestic." (James Wong recorded)'}

{'index': 30, 'translation': "A lifetime's attachments — the world of drama"}

{'index': 31, 'translation': 'That year, watching King Sir\'s "Cyrano de Bergerac," at the final scene in the pitch-black theatre, I sat in the center of the front row, as if witnessing the end of the world alone, letting tears flow freely, my heart churning. Returning to my inner self, what life ultimately needs, and what it possesses day after day, are forever separated by countless mountains. "Cyrano de Bergerac" conveys the essence of tragedy through humor: a rare and precious achievement. A lifetime\'s attachments, a lifetime\'s pursuit — that is life. The mind is free. Apart from being moved, I also realized for myself —'}

{'index': 32, 'translation': 'What is theatre? At that moment, theatre was a place that allowed me to look forward in the darkness. One need not become an actor, yet one must earnestly pursue the greatest good and beauty. I missed the Academy of Performing Arts, lost certain things, but was actually moving toward another possibility. What matters most is that you still clearly know what you long for.'}

{'index': 33, 'translation': 'King Sir\'s stage works opened my eyes greatly. One of his early works at the Academy of Performing Arts, "Under the Banyan Tree," is likewise a wonderful original play full of Hong Kong\'s local color. In junior secondary school I had already heard of his directings of "Equus," "Mozart\'s Death," "Death of a Salesman," and "West Side Story" — I never had the chance to see them. What is even more regrettable is that I never had the opportunity to sit down with King Sir for a long conversation about drama and life. More than ten years ago, through the late PolyU journalism director Lai Ming-fai...'}

{'index': 34, 'translation': '"Whether interacting with peers or young people, he was always modest and courteous, with a gentle smile. That was not put on; it was the inner cultivation of a true gentleman, making one feel respected yet at ease."'}

{'index': 35, 'translation': 'The above passage, from the citation when Hong Kong Shue Yan University conferred an honorary doctorate on King Sir in 2018, resonates particularly with me. From my own brief encounters with King Sir, his smile and the way he looked at you made one feel deeply respected, warming the heart. I personally suspect that he did not accept interviews because of the strained relationship between the television station and the newspaper where I worked at the time.'}

{'index': 36, 'translation': 'Back then, when I thought about applying to the Academy of Performing Arts, everyone assumed I dreamed of becoming an actor and entering the stage. I immediately responded: "No, I want to study drama." That could be the world of directing, playwriting, or literature. From junior secondary school, I had written two or three scripts myself, writing, directing and acting in them, but that fire eventually died out, quietly buried deep in my heart — once a lingering regret.'}

{'index': 37, 'translation': 'Four years ago, when writing about Dickens on Patreon, I read several relevant academic articles and finally understood how Dickens transformed from missing out on opportunities to be an actor and a journalist into the literary giant of his era. I gained a new understanding of the dream I had treasured for so many years.'}

{'index': 38, 'translation': 'In his later years, Dickens performed his own works in person — live readings that he wrote and directed himself — and the ticket revenue exceeded that from his novels, with more than half his wealth coming from this (see the first Patreon article). He sublimated the passion for performing from his youth into the opportunity to read his own works aloud. The wonder of life lies not in realizing dreams, but in transformation and sublimation. Drama teaches life\'s most important lesson: called "a blessing in disguise." Sometimes love cannot be obtained...'}

{'index': 39, 'translation': "Last year in England, I passed by Dickens's former residence in Rochester. It is said that Dickens's father once encouraged his son to study hard so that one day he could buy a house like that. Dickens eventually did buy this house, which has been preserved to this day, with a secondary school attached beside it — the students there are truly blessed."}

{'index': 40, 'translation': 'Life is like a play; one need not lament its twists and turns, for there may be too much worth appreciating. Once I understood this, I poured my passion into free self-expression and became a journalist who loves to write stories about people. I invest my deepest feelings into true stories — stories with you, with me, with him — play after play of "stages built from words." If they can move people\'s hearts, that is the warmest applause.'}

{'index': 41, 'translation': "The founding and golden years of the Academy of Performing Arts — Hong Kong's Academy of Performing Arts has been established for more than forty years. At its founding, there were only four schools: Drama, Music, Dance, and Stage Technology (Technical Arts). Later Film and Television and Cantonese Opera were added, making six in total. Looking back at this academy I once failed to enter, in the mid-eighties, no university campus could be so grand and elegant, with air conditioning running all day. To maintain the venue and equipment, every corner was kept fresh and cool. The brand-new campus (to be continued)."}

{'index': 42, 'translation': 'In the first few years after the academy was founded, for various reasons, I often lingered in countless corners of this "great playground." To be honest, the first time I walked in, I felt tiny and out of place — not because the place was big, but because the atmosphere was so far removed from our daily lives, yet open to everyone. Students from different backgrounds and social classes gathered to learn together, united by shared interests and ideals. It was a very special way of life, yet not out of reach.'}

{'index': 43, 'translation': 'Whether King Sir (King Chung) can become a master depends on whether we have inherited the environment that nurtured masters. The academy has developed for forty-two years; Hong Kong has established a system and standards for the performing arts. Drama culture has not only borne fruit through different theatre companies, but has also taken root in the free atmosphere of the Academy of Performing Arts. King Sir is an iconic founding figure. Since his era, many professionals dedicated to drama education, along with their students...'}
